subject: Rapid SLO clarification: input/output window ceilings & streaming expectations

Subject: Rapid SLO clarification: input/output window ceilings & streaming expectations

Hi Sam & Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size a POC correctly:

Summary of what I heard on requirements: 
- Latency target: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300 ms for the live chat use case (single-turn inference) — target for production; POC can accept 95th <= 400 ms.
- Throughput/conc: expected peak concurrent users ~120, burst QPS ~180 for short bursts (~5 minutes).
- Streaming: yes — front-end expects token streaming for progressive rendering, and client-side cancellation for user edits.
- Context: typical input (customer message + 2 messages history) ~1.2k tokens; expected output average ~220 tokens, worst-case output up to ~1.8k tokens for long-form summaries.

Questions that will affect model & infra selection: 
1) For the long-form summaries (worst-case ~1.8k output) — how often does that happen? (rough frequency % of requests)
2) Are you willing to accept an explicit output cap (e.g., server truncation at 1024 tokens) if we show fallbacks like streaming partial summary + follow-up generation?
3) Do you have an SLA requirement for tail latency during bursts, or is the 95th baseline sufficient?

Immediate next steps I propose: 
- I’ll share a compact SLO matrix (attached) that maps context+output ceilings to model variants, expected p95/p99 ranges, and recommended concurrency/batch settings.
- Schedule a 1-hour technical sizing with Karthik to walk through KV cache behavior with your prompt shapes and the streaming handshake. Please share two example sessions (raw input + expected full output) — Priya, can you attach 2 anonymized transcripts?

Thanks — I want to make sure we’re not undershooting token ceilings that drive tail latency.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Rapid SLO clarification: input/output window ceilings & streaming expectations

Neha — thanks, helpful summary. A few clarifications below (answering your numbered points):

1) Long-form summaries (~1.8k outputs) are relatively rare — ~3-5% of sessions. Most replies are 100–300 tokens.
2) We would prefer server-side soft caps rather than hard cuts — if you can stream a partial summary and then continue on demand that’s fine. Hard truncation feels risky for compliance.
3) The customer-facing SLA we promise is 99.5% availability and p95 latency targets — but internal ops will tolerate p99 up to 2× p95 during short bursts. We’ll need to understand what that means for model choice.

A couple more details:
- Cancellation: our UI cancels when users edit within 700 ms of seeing first tokens ~10% of sessions. We’d like the server to release KV cache and not charge for partially streamed tokens if cancelled early.
- Auth: tokens are per-session; we will need to route some high-privileged customer sessions to dedicated capacity (separate from the multi-tenant pool) — likely 4–8 GPUs for initial POC.

If Karthik wants to dig into exact prompt shapes I can share two anonymized transcripts by EOD. Otherwise, schedule the sizing and we’ll be there.

— Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Product, OpsLyft

Thanks Sam — that frequency % is very helpful. A few technical notes from our side ahead of the sizing call so we can come prepared with a concrete POC plan: 

- Model variants: for the mixed workload you described (mostly short outputs + rare long-form) we typically recommend a smaller quantized variant for the multi-tenant pool to serve ~90% of traffic and a larger non-quantized variant pinned to dedicated GPUs for the 3-5% long-form/priority sessions. This reduces unit cost while keeping tail latency guarantees for priority traffic.

- Streaming semantics & charging: Redwood can support token streaming with an event-based billing hook. We can configure cancellation semantics to prorate billing for partially-streamed responses and optionally release KV cache immediately on cancel. We should capture this in the mutual action plan.

- Tail latency hedges: to handle bursty p99 spikes we suggest a fallback policy: if p95 rises above 300 ms for >30s, route new sessions to the dedicated variant (if capacity exists) or to a lower-cost capped variant that streams partial answers and offers a continued background generation (we call this progressive-answer fallback).

- Token ceiling options:
  * Conservative plan: server output cap 1024 tokens; progressive-answer flow for >1024 (keeps latency predictable).
  * Aggressive plan: allow up to 2048 output tokens on dedicated capacity; use streaming + soft-stop threshold at 1800 tokens to reduce tail cost.

Action items: 
- Priya: please attach two anonymized transcripts (one short chat, one long-form), and indicate which sessions are priority customers to map to dedicated capacity.
- Karthik/Neha: we will prepare an ops-level POC runbook detailing load profiles (ramping to 180 QPS, sustained 120 QPS), expected p95/p99 ranges per model variant, and recommended autoscale triggers.
- Marissa: follow up on procurement/contract lead time for dedicated GPUs so we can propose a calendar.

Proposed scheduling: Karthik and I are available Thu 5/27 at 10:00 AM PT or Fri 5/28 at 9:00 AM PT for the technical sizing. Which works?

— Neha
